interrogator_dossier:
# Yelp Inc. (YELP) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-10-26 from five earnings calls (Q2 2025, reported 2025-08-08, through Q2 2026, reported 2026-08-06) and the screener's financial history. Price used: $19.99 (NYSE, USD, from the screener scan; the live quote service was unreachable today).*

**Bottom line.** Yelp is a highly profitable, cash-rich local-advertising business whose core advertising engine has stopped growing. Management has been reliable on its own short-term guidance (it beat the top of its revenue and profit ranges in every one of the five calls), but the story it tells has shifted in twelve months from "services advertising drives our growth" to "new AI products will reaccelerate us." The numbers support the cash story and do not yet support the growth story.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q2 2025 (2025-08-08):** a confident, record-quarter call. "Record net revenue and strong profitability"; services advertising up 8% year over year was "driving our business performance"; restaurants, retail and other (RR&O) down 5%, blamed on macro. AI was a product feature (Yelp Assistant, data licensing at a ">$10 million" annual run rate).
- **Q3 2025 (2025-11-06):** same framing, but the full-year revenue range was cut by $8 million at the midpoint and management said Q4 revenue would fall from Q3. New voice-AI subscription products (Yelp Host, Yelp Receptionist) and a DoorDash food-ordering deal introduced.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-13):** the story pivots to "transforming Yelp with AI." Three new strategic pillars (conversational discovery, AI tools for businesses, licensing content to AI platforms), the acquisition of Hatch (an AI lead-management tool for service pros), an OpenAI licensing deal. Yelp Receptionist was quietly dropped in favour of Hatch.
- **Q1 2026 (2026-05-08):** revenue +1%, services advertising +1%, RR&O -11%, net income -27%. The new headline target: $250 million annual run rate of "Other revenue" (AI products, licensing, food ordering) by end-2028, more than double the Q1 run rate.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-08-06):** revenue +1%, services advertising flat, RR&O -10%, net income -28%. Capital allocation changes: acquisitions "through a combination of cash and financing," at least 50% of free cash flow returned through buybacks, and buybacks paused to pay down the revolving credit line, resuming in 2027.

The drift is clear: the growth driver moved from the core advertising business (now flat) to a small, fast-growing side business that is under 10% of revenue.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Strong profitability" and margin potential | Net margin 9.9% in fiscal 2025; adjusted EBITDA margin 25% in 2025, 22% in Q1 2026 and 24% in Q2 2026; free cash flow (cash from operations minus capital spending) $297M over the twelve months to 2026-06-30, a 22% margin | Holds on cash; GAAP net income is falling (-27% and -28% in the last two quarters) |
| Services advertising is the growth engine | +8% (Q2 2025), +7% (Q3 2025), +1% (Q1 2026), 0% (Q2 2026) | Does not hold now. The engine has stalled |
| Other revenue will reach $250M run rate by end-2028 | $29M in Q1 2026 (+75%), $33M in Q2 2026 (+98%, flattered by the Hatch acquisition); Hatch growth slowed from 92% (March) to 59% (June) | Plausible direction, but it needs the run rate to roughly double again in 2.5 years, and part of today's growth is bought |
| Stock-based pay is being cut | 9% of revenue in Q2 2025 to 7% in Q2 2026; target under 6% by end-2027 | Holds - a real quality improvement |
| Buybacks shrink the share base | Fully diluted shares fell from 86M (end-2021) to 67M (end-2025); diluted shares -15% year over year at Q2 2026 | Holds, but the shares were bought at $32-36 in 2025 and ~$25 in Q2 2026 - well above today's $20 |
| Healthy balance sheet | Net debt of about $29M at 2026-06-30 including leases (borrowings $100M plus $23M leases, minus $94M cash), versus a large net cash position in earlier years | Weaker than before: management borrowed and paused buybacks to repay it |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable-to-declining on the core, rising on the new products.** The 2025 calls opened with "record net revenue." By Q1 2026 the opener was "local businesses have continued to face a challenging economic environment," and in Q2 2026 the chief operating officer said "we don't expect any massive trajectory turn in terms of the broader local economy." Guidance language turned defensive ("the degree of uncertainty that we need to reflect," Q1 2026). Meanwhile language on AI products became more expansive ("considerable opportunity," "potentially significant distribution channel").

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Revenue beat the top of the guided range in every call reviewed: +$3M (Q2 2025), +$6M (Q3 2025), +$6M (Q1 2026), +$8M (Q2 2026); adjusted EBITDA beat by $11-16M.
